_comment: PRD §9 'Dynamic events' — all ten MVP events from the §9 table. `baseball_game_ends` reproduces the §16 'Event definition example' field for field and value for value, and its `effects` keys are the vocabulary every other event follows: footTrafficMultiplier, segmentWeightOverrides, dishTagDemandMultipliers, partySizeMultiplier. Four §9 events describe consequences that vocabulary cannot express (rain raising dine-in patience, a critic party, a slow restock, slowed equipment), so those carry one or two clearly-named extra keys; the four §16 keys are still present on every event so a consumer can read them unconditionally. `durationMs` is the §9 table's duration. `warningMs` is the §9 'teaser or forecast appears 10-20 seconds before activation when appropriate' lead time; it is 0 for the two events nothing in the district would telegraph. segmentWeightOverrides REPLACES the market's weight for the named segment while the event is active; the remaining weight is redistributed proportionally across the segments not named. All multipliers are 1.0-relative: > 1 amplifies, < 1 dampens.

events.title: Office Break Starts
events.description: The towers empty out. Fast, cheap and predictable wins the next minute.

events.title: Theater Curtain Call
events.description: Curtain is up in minutes. Upscale diners want quality without a long sitting.

events.title: Baseball Game Ends
events.description: Expect a large surge of hungry groups. Shareable dishes and quick service are in demand.

events.title: Rainstorm
events.description: Foot traffic thins, but the guests already inside are in no hurry to leave.

events.title: Food Critic Spotted
events.description: A high-value critic party is approaching. Exceptional service can be worth more than the check.

events.title: Ingredient Shortage
events.description: A supplier is short. One ingredient restocks slower and costs more until it clears.

events.title: Local Influencer Post
events.description: A post is circulating. Signature and shareable dishes are suddenly in demand.

events.title: Transit Delay
events.description: Arrivals stall, then land all at once. Idle labour now, a queue in a minute.

events.title: Happy Hour Nearby
events.description: The bars next door just cut their prices. Value-hunting groups spill over.

events.title: Power Fluctuation
events.description: The grid dips. Heated equipment runs slow until it steadies.
